editorial.headline: Immersive Media Development, From Code to Experience
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the making and upkeep of VR, AR and MR software and immersive content—open nationally to foreign ownership, with a distinct Bali risk picture at large scale.
editorial.body:
Immersive media is not a loose label here. It names the programming and application-development work behind VR, AR, and MR experiences: designing their structure and content; writing, modifying, updating, patching, customising and testing code; and providing technical support as the software is implemented. The category also reaches the creation or customisation of digital material designed specifically for immersive use, including three-dimensional visuals, 360-degree video, and their modifications. The link is functional: the content is made or adapted to be displayed and operated through immersive media, alongside the software that enables it.

That makes the registrant profile broader than a studio that merely supplies an image or video. It is for the party building or adapting the application and its purpose-built immersive content, and then supporting the code in operation. The record opens this activity to Micro, Small, Medium and Large business scales, so its stated scope does not reserve the work for a single company size. Its boundary is equally useful: software-needs consulting and advisory work is outside this activity. The focus is the applied, technical work of developing, altering, testing, implementing and supporting immersive software and its specific content.

Nationally, this is a TERBUKA activity for PMA with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. In plain terms, the record allows foreign ownership to reach 100%; it does not record a lower national cap for this activity. That national position should be read alongside, rather than substituted for, the Bali view. Bali's standing is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says that at the Large scale the OSS risk is Medium-High/High. It also says that this risk position does not block the activity under the Bali moratorium.

Bali's permanent PMA moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities island-wide. This activity is not blocked by that rule. The distinction matters: the national foreign-ownership setting and the Bali risk statement are separate parts of the record, and neither overrides the other. The honest reading is clean: a foreign investor has a nationally open activity with up to 100% foreign ownership, while Bali does not bar its PMA registration under the stated moratorium. At Large scale, its OSS risk is expressly Medium-High/High—a classification in the Bali record, not a Bali prohibition.
